questions.question_text: What TWO distinctly American traditions have contributed their own unique emphasis to the field of dynamic psychotherapy with children, particularly play therapy?
questions.explanation: The child guidance movement and client-centered therapy contributed to the development of dynamic play therapy with children, but it should not be equated with child psychoanalytic therapy.

questions.question_text: Findings from large-scale epidemiological studies examining individuals with mental retardation (MR) show ALL of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Rates of MR are generally low in the early years
More boys than girls have MR
Rates of MR peak at around 10 to 14 years
Individuals of lower socioeconomic status (SES) show higher than expected rates of MR
Rates of MR stay constant during adulthood

correct_answer.text: Rates of MR stay constant during adulthood

correct_answers.text: Rates of MR stay constant during adulthood

questions.explanation: Additional findings have also recently been reported from large-scale epidemiological studies. For individuals with severe mental retardation (MR), prevalence levels mostly converge on 3 to 4 children per 1,000; for mild MR, rates range wildly from 5.4 to 10.6 children per 1,000. Studies also examine such correlates as gender, age, and socioeconomic status. More boys than girls have MR, and rates of MR are generally low in the early years, peak at around 10 to 14 years, and decrease slightly in the late-school years and markedly during adulthood. Individuals of lower socioeconomic status and of ethnic minority groups (in several cultures) also show higher than expected rates of MR.

questions.question_text: Which of the following learning disabilities (LDs) currently has the most research on relevant genes and brain structure and brain function to support a neurobiological base for LDs?
questions.explanation: Far more research on relevant genes and brain structure and function is available for children with specific reading disability than for any other learning disability.

questions.question_text: Approximately what percentage of pediatric patients in primary care have mental health problems?
questions.explanation: Approximately 15% to 25% of pediatric patients are thought to have mental health problems.

Family factors seem to be stronger predictors of psychopathology than epilepsy factors
Children with epilepsy experience more frequent difficulties in reading, writing, and mathematics than controls
Epilepsy can be associated with a decrease in intelligence quotient (IQ) for a subset of children

questions.explanation: It is important to note that some of the above findings reflect group trends, and many individuals with epilepsy do exceedingly well in all areas. options.text: Homozygosity for the long allele of the serotonin transporter gene and negative life events
Homozygosity for the long allele of the serotonin transporter gene
Homozygosity for the short allele of the serotonin transporter gene
Homozygosity for the short allele of the serotonin transporter gene and negative life events

questions.explanation: This was one of the first examples of the importance of gene–environment interaction.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes the hypothesized mechanism of action of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)?

options.text: Selectively promotes the release of newly synthesized dopamine while also blocking dopamine reuptake at the transporter
Promotes the release of serotonin in the prefrontal cortex
Interferes with the return of serotonin into the presynaptic neuron
Interferes with the return of serotonin into the postsynaptic neuron
Promotes the release of stored dopamine and blocks the return of dopamine at presynaptic dopamine transporter sites.

correct_answer.text: Interferes with the return of serotonin into the presynaptic neuron

correct_answers.text: Interferes with the return of serotonin into the presynaptic neuron

questions.explanation: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) block the serotonin transporter located on presynaptic nerve terminals. Over time, this blockade leads to a desensitization of the serotonin autoreceptors, which typically exert an inhibitory influence on serotonin release; consequently, serotonergic function is enhanced.

The risks and consequences of each of the following: the proposed treatment, the alternative treatments, and no treatment
The nature, purpose, and benefits of the proposed treatment and the probability that it will succeed

questions.explanation: In place of informed consent, permission of one or both parents or a legal guardian is required (permission to treat) as well as the agreement (assent) of the child.

questions.question_text: True or False: All drugs undergoing hepatic and intestinal biotransformation must be metabolized in a Phase I reaction prior to undergoing conjugation by Phase II enzymes.
questions.explanation: Drugs such as the 3-hydroxybenzodiazepines (lorazepam, oxazepam, and temazepam) as well as lamotrigine are not metabolized by Phase I reactions, but are conjugated by glucuronidation only.
